theme: Actor hops, isolated parameters and sending parameters

terms.definition: A switch of a task from one actor's executor to another when it awaits a call on that actor.
terms.example: Each actor hop costs a little time.

terms.definition: A function parameter marked `isolated`, so the function runs inside that actor's isolation.
terms.example: Make it an isolated parameter to skip the await.

terms.definition: A parameter marked `sending`, which hands the value over so the caller cannot use it afterward.
terms.example: Pass a new object through a sending parameter.

Learn to explain how to reduce actor hops and hand values to actors safely: Actor Hop, Isolated Parameter & Sending Parameter, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Actor Hop - A switch of a task from one actor's executor to another when it awaits a call on that actor.
Isolated Parameter - A function parameter marked `isolated`, so the function runs inside that actor's isolation.
Sending Parameter - A parameter marked `sending`, which hands the value over so the caller cannot use it afterward.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Actor Hop, Isolated Parameter and Sending Parameter in English?

dialogue.title: Too many hops
dialogue.setting: A loop with many awaits on one actor

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my loop changes `c.n` with ten separate await calls, and it feels slow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Each await call is an actor hop. An actor hop switches the task to the actor's executor.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use an isolated parameter, like in `bump`. An isolated parameter runs the whole function inside the actor.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So with an isolated parameter I do not need await inside `bump`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. You pay for one actor hop at the call, and then the loop is free.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nice. What about passing a class into an actor?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A class is not safe to share, so use a sending parameter.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What does a sending parameter do?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It hands the value over to the actor. After that the caller cannot use it again.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That prevents two places from changing the same object.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. The compiler checks every sending parameter for you.
Each actor hop costs a little time.
